newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota's madcap mayor resigns to run for presidency.
newsitem.headline: Bogota's madcap mayor resigns to run for presidency.

text.p: Bogota's madcap mayor Antanas Mockus handed in his resignation on Saturday in readiness to run in next year's presidential elections.
Under Colombian law anybody seeking to run for the presidency must resign from public office a year before elections, which are scheduled for May 1998.

Mockus, whose headline grabbing antics include baring his backside in public and getting married in a tigers' cage, said he would give President Ernesto Samper a list of possible successors and be out of City Hall by mid-April.
Mockus, a self-described "neo-anarchist" and academic with a passion for mathematics and metaphysics, took office in January 1995 for a two-year term.
The mayor has done little to solve Bogota's infrastructure and chronic traffic problems or cut soaring crime rates but has scored consistently well in voter opinion polls.

Political analysts see his popularity as symptomatic of the need for change in a country torn by drugs and violence where two parties, Samper's Liberals and the opposition Conservatives, have shared jealously-guarded power since a bloody civil war that ended in 1958.

It was initially thought Mockus may run for the vice- presidency on a joint ticket with Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso. But Valdivieso has denied cutting any deal with the Bogota mayor and has not even declared if he will stand.
